name: Obrábění Kraslin s.r.o.
summary: Obrábění Kraslin is a founder-owned Czech machining shop (30 staff, 2-5 M EUR turnover, founded 2008) and the 100 % single source for adapter piece part:320050 at 15.88 EUR. The owner negotiates personally, remembers that he held the old price for a quarter in 2022, and expects partnership in return. Its delivery and quality scorecard has been amber for four quarters (OTD 84.6 % against a 95 % target, 1531 ppm), though it is improving, and its sales side is reviewing small accounts to focus on customers with volume.

situation.decision_maker: owner (founder) decides price; sales director drives account prioritisation

negotiation_pattern: Opens with moderate asks (+2.8 %, +5.8 %) and settles well below them (0.0 %, +2.7 %). The average gap between ask and settlement is -2.4 points. In 2023 he even offered a decrease (-4.1 %) and accepted -5.4 %. He frames talks in terms of reciprocity and past favours rather than hard data. His cost basis is a personal spreadsheet last updated two years ago, and he questioned where our index figures come from. He has not used his contractual price-notice window aggressively.
wants: being treated as a partner (recognition of the 2022 price hold)
on-time payment (we pay late 85 % of the time)
volume and continuity security (contract extension, forecasts)
modest price increase to cover costs
protects: fairness and reciprocity: will dig in if pressured or lectured
unit_price below cost as he sees it (hard 0 % was already conceded last round)
the account itself: may drop small/low-margin customers rather than give more

trades.give: payment_days: commit to genuinely paying on time at 45 days (stop the average 5.4 days late)
trades.why: Fixes a real fairness grievance at near-zero cost to us. For a reciprocity-driven owner, it is worth more than its interest value.

trades.give: contract_months: extend the framework beyond 2027-06-30 (e.g. +12-24 months) plus a rolling volume forecast
trades.get: price hold or a capped increase of 1 % or less
trades.why: The supplier is screening out small accounts. Committed continuity keeps us in the 'volume customer' group.

trades.give: index_clause: offer a transparent, jointly agreed public index with a deadband, and share our data sources
trades.get: drop ad-hoc annual increase asks; settle 2027 on index facts
trades.why: The owner's spreadsheet is two years old and he asked about our sources. Shared data builds trust and anchors the price on facts.

trades.give: chargeback_eur_per_complaint: keep the 150 EUR flat fee unchanged (no escalation)
trades.get: ppm_commitment below 1000 and an OTD improvement plan toward the 95 % target
trades.why: The trend is improving but still amber. A cooperative fix-plan fits the relationship better than penalties.

arguments.point: We acknowledge the 2022 quarter at the old price and want a long-term partnership. Here is what we offer in return: on-time payment and an extended contract.
Last year closed at 0 % and the price is fixed per calendar year. Any 2027 change needs written notice 90 days before year-end, i.e. by early October 2026.
Delivery is still far from the agreed 95 % OTD (84.6 %) and ppm is around 1500. Price discussion should go hand in hand with continued improvement.
Offer to walk him through the current index data. His figures are two years old, and updated numbers may not justify a large increase.

avoid: Threatening resourcing or using the tooling ownership as a club in the opening: it triggers digging in from a founder who expects partnership.
Condescension about his outdated spreadsheet; offer data as help instead.
Demanding longer payment terms while we already pay late most of the time.
Treating Hollerau as a small account that asks a lot and gives little, given he is pruning small customers.
tone: Personal, respectful, owner-to-partner. Acknowledge history, be factual and fair, firm but never aggressive.
red_flags: Single source (100 % quota, no other sources) for part:320050; a walk-away would hurt us, though we own the tooling.
Supplier is reviewing small accounts; Hollerau could be deprioritised or dropped.
Persistent amber scorecard: OTD 84.6 % vs 95 % target, ppm 1531.
Our chronic late payment (85 % late) undermines the partnership narrative and could fuel a price push.
The 90-day notice window for a 2027 change expires within days; expect a late increase request.

evidence.claim: Founder-owned s.r.o., 30 staff, 2-5 M EUR turnover; credit index stable at 245, equity ratio 44.8 % (no cash stress).
Owner reminded us of the 2022 quarter at the old price and expects partnership.
Sales director is reviewing small accounts and focusing on volume customers.
Owner uses his own index spreadsheet, last updated two years ago.
Renewal history: asked +2.8 % and settled 0.0 %; asked +5.8 % and settled +2.7 %; asked -4.1 % and settled -5.4 %.
Scorecard amber for four quarters; OTD improving from 73.1 % to 84.6 %, ppm 1531 in the latest quarter.
Contract: prices fixed per calendar year with 90-day notice before year-end, 45 days net, EXW, 150 EUR per complaint, runs to 2027-06-30 with auto-extension.
Single source with 100 % quota and no alternatives, but Hollerau owns the tooling.

indicators.credit_index: 245 (12 months ago 245; higher is worse, >300 weak)
indicators.scorecard_trend: 2025Q4 amber (otd 73.1, ppm 1557) → 2026Q1 amber (otd 74.1, ppm 1937) → 2026Q2 amber (otd 78.6, ppm 1661) → 2026Q3 amber (otd 84.6, ppm 1531)
